stories.title: Government seeks more time for AI 171 crash report
stories.summary: The central government has asked the Supreme Court for another extension to publish the final investigation report into the Air India Flight 171 crash. Officials stated the report is in its final stage. The crash occurred in June 2025, killing 241 people.

stories.title: IndiGo suspends Saudi Arabia flights until November 30
stories.summary: IndiGo has cancelled all flights to and from Jeddah, Riyadh, Madinah, and Dammam until November 30. The airline cited regional security tensions and ballistic missile interceptions as the cause. Bookings remain paused while the carrier manages affected passengers.

stories.title: Air India Express appoints Deepak Rajawat as CEO
stories.summary: Deepak Rajawat will become the Chief Executive Officer of Air India Express on December 1. Rajawat, who previously served as the airline's Chief Financial Officer, aims to create a customer-centric organization. He is tasked with navigating challenges in the evolving aviation sector.

stories.title: SpiceJet faces operational crisis as cancellations mount
stories.summary: SpiceJet is cancelling over 50 percent of its daily flights due to a cash shortage following a loan rejection. Airline executives warned of a potential shutdown if funds are not secured within a week. The regulator has yet to restrict the carrier from taking new bookings.

stories.title: SpiceJet cancels over half of daily flights
stories.summary: SpiceJet has cancelled most flights out of Mumbai, leaving thousands stranded as the airline faces a severe cash shortage. The board has cleared a fundraise of 5,500 crore rupees. Despite the operational instability, the regulator continues to allow the airline to accept new customer bookings.

stories.title: Supreme Court grants more time for AI 171 report
stories.summary: The government has requested another two or three weeks to publish the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau report on the Air India Flight 171 crash. The investigation into the 2025 accident was previously expected by late October. Officials describe the report as being at the fag end.

stories.title: IndiGo aircraft grounded after bird strike
stories.summary: An IndiGo flight from Mangaluru was grounded for inspection after a bird strike at Navi Mumbai Airport on Tuesday. The incident marks the airline's second operational disruption of the day. The carrier is currently navigating an ongoing FAA audit of India's aviation safety standards.

stories.title: Bengaluru-bound IndiGo flight aborts take-off in Mangaluru after technical snag, 236 safely deplaned - Telegraph India
IndiGo halts Saudi Arabia routes through November
stories.summary: IndiGo has suspended all flights connecting India to Jeddah, Riyadh, Madinah, and Dammam until November 30. The airline confirmed the move follows regional security concerns. Similar suspensions have been implemented by other carriers operating in the region.

stories.title: IndiGo and other airlines suspend Saudi Arabia flights
stories.summary: IndiGo, Air India, and Akasa Air have suspended flights to Jeddah, Madinah, Riyadh, and Dammam until November 30. The airlines cited security concerns in the region as the primary reason for the cancellations. Specific details regarding the nature of the threats were not provided.

stories.title: IndiGo cancels Saudi Arabia flights amid security concerns
stories.summary: IndiGo has cancelled all flights to and from Jeddah, Madinah, Riyadh, and Dammam until November 30. The airline cited the prevailing security situation following reports of ballistic missiles launched by Houthi rebels. Passengers are being notified of the service disruptions and offered assistance.

stories.title: Southwest Airlines stroller damage policy questioned
stories.summary: A passenger reports that Southwest Airlines refused to pay for a damaged stroller, claiming the carrier was not liable for damages to checked items. The airline maintains it is only responsible for lost items. The passenger's experience has prompted public questions regarding airline baggage liability.

stories.title: Delta to end lounge access for Basic Business fares
stories.summary: Delta Air Lines has launched a Basic Business fare that retains lie-flat seats but removes lounge access starting January 19, 2027. The lower-priced ticket also restricts seat selection and frequent flyer earnings. Premium travelers are being asked to trade benefits for a lower entry price.

IndiGo suspends Saudi flights citing regional tensions
stories.summary: IndiGo has cancelled all flights to and from Jeddah, Madinah, Riyadh, and Dammam until November 30. The airline stated the decision is due to the security situation in Saudi Arabia as tensions with Houthi rebels intensify. Affected passengers are being contacted regarding their bookings.

stories.title: Airbus aims for 250 deliveries in final two months of 2026
stories.summary: Airbus plans to hand over roughly 250 aircraft in November and December to meet its annual delivery target. Commercial aircraft head Lars Wagner stated every one of these planes is already in final assembly or on delivery lines. The planemaker is counting on its factory floors to deliver.

stories.title: American Airlines expands Airbus narrowbody fleet
stories.summary: American Airlines has increased its Airbus A321neo fleet to 90 aircraft. The carrier expects two more standard A321neos and one A321XLR by the end of 2026. With no further Boeing deliveries scheduled this year, Airbus remains the primary source for the airline's near-term fleet renewal.

stories.title: Malaysia Airlines considers Boeing Dreamliner order
stories.summary: Malaysia Airlines is evaluating an order for up to 20 Boeing Dreamliners. The carrier is targeting deliveries for the new widebody aircraft by 2030.

stories.title: Philippine Airlines adds to A350 fleet
stories.summary: Philippine Airlines is expanding its widebody fleet with two additional Airbus A350-1000s. The carrier expects the next delivery in early December, with the following aircraft arriving around January 1, 2027, according to CEO Richard Nuttall.

stories.title: UAC secures order for six Il-114-300 turboprops
stories.summary: Russia's United Aircraft Corporation has secured an order for six Ilyushin Il-114-300 regional turboprops from Polar Airlines. Five aircraft are scheduled for delivery in 2029, with the final unit arriving in 2030.

stories.title: Philippine Airlines firms up 15 Boeing 787-10 order
stories.summary: Philippine Airlines has finalized an agreement for 15 Boeing 787-10 Dreamliners, with options for five additional jets. The deal marks the carrier's largest widebody purchase to date and fulfills a commitment announced in July 2026. The aircraft will be powered by GE Aerospace GEnx-1B engines.

stories.title: Middle East Airlines receives first Airbus A321XLR
stories.summary: Middle East Airlines has taken delivery of its first Airbus A321XLR, seven years after placing the initial order. The carrier, which was the launch customer for the type, had its deliveries delayed from 2023-24. Other airlines have since put the aircraft into service.

stories.title: Philippine Airlines finalizes 15-plane Dreamliner order
stories.summary: Philippine Airlines has finalized its order for 15 Boeing 787-10 Dreamliners, including options for five more. The 787-10, which seats up to 375 passengers, represents the flag carrier's largest widebody purchase. The order follows a commitment made by the airline in July 2026.

stories.title: Airbus delivers first A321XLR to Middle East Airlines
stories.summary: Airbus delivered the first A321XLR to Middle East Airlines on November 17, 2026. While the Lebanese carrier was the launch customer for the aircraft, it was not the first to put the type into service. That distinction went to Iberia earlier this month.

FAA official signed off on router work before ground stop
stories.summary: An FAA official oversaw and signed off on a router replacement and fiber-optic cable installation in Arkansas shortly before the nationwide ground stop on November 13. The work was part of a broader infrastructure upgrade effort. The agency has not commented on the timing.

stories.title: FAA requests $50.1 billion for system overhaul
stories.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and FAA officials have requested $50.1 billion to modernize air traffic control systems. The proposal follows a four-hour nationwide ground stop on November 13 caused by aging equipment. A previous $12.5 billion allocation from 2025 is already fully committed.

stories.title: FAA outage ruled out as cyberattack
stories.summary: Federal officials have confirmed that the recent FAA technology failure, which grounded flights nationwide, was not the result of a coordinated cyberattack. The disruption occurred during a technology upgrade. Lawmakers are now scrutinizing the resilience of the nation's digital aviation infrastructure.

stories.title: Duckworth proposes modernization bill following FAA outage
stories.summary: Senator Tammy Duckworth has introduced legislation to modernize air traffic control systems following the nationwide FAA ground stop on November 13. The proposal seeks to address concerns regarding the resilience and security of the agency's digital infrastructure after a technical malfunction disrupted thousands of flights.

stories.title: Ground Stop Came as Duffy Pushed to Rapidly Upgrade Aviation Systems - The New York Times
FAA identifies cause of nationwide ground stop
stories.summary: The FAA confirmed that a technical problem caused the November 13 nationwide ground stop, which lasted 4 hours and 40 minutes. The agency stated the incident was not the result of a cyberattack. It marks only the second such halt since September 11, 2001.

stories.title: F.A.A. Shelves Routers Like the One Linked to the Nationwide Ground Stop - The New York Times
Morocco commits $3 million to train 300 African aviation inspectors
stories.summary: Morocco will invest $3 million to train 300 civil aviation inspectors from Africa over three years. The program, run in partnership with the International Civil Aviation Organization, aims to strengthen regulatory capabilities across the continent. Morocco intends to become a key aviation partner for the region.

stories.title: North Carolina community colleges collaborate to train aviation workforce
stories.summary: Seven community colleges in North Carolina are partnering to train students for careers in aerospace and aviation. The initiative aims to provide the workforce required by companies currently operating in the Piedmont Triad. The industry is reportedly looking to revolutionize the sector in the region.

US Air Force pilot training hits 1,518 graduates
stories.summary: The US Air Force graduated 1,518 new pilots in fiscal 2026, surpassing its annual goal of 1,500. According to Lt. Gen. Clark J. Quinn, this is the highest number of graduates in 35 years. The last time the service reached this milestone was in 1991.

stories.title: Paragon Flight Training receives FAA authorization for nationwide check rides
stories.summary: Paragon Flight Training is the first flight school in the US to receive Airman Certification Organization Designation Authorization from the FAA. The school is now permitted to conduct check rides for its own students and those from other flight schools nationwide. The authorization took effect November 11.

stories.title: New aviation security training pathway opens at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport
stories.summary: The Port of Seattle has launched a new training pathway for aviation security professionals at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. The program covers employee screening, physical security operations, and cargo safety. It is intended to help new recruits enter the field and support the airport's existing security infrastructure.

stories.title: Romania accepts first upgraded IAR-99 jet trainers
stories.summary: Romania has accepted the first two of 10 modernized IAR-99 SM jet trainers from Avioane Craiova. The aircraft were delivered on November 16, more than two years after the original deadline. They will support pilot training for the F-16 fighter at the Air Force Application School.

stories.title: ATP Flight School expands to Lehigh Valley International Airport
stories.summary: ATP Flight School has opened a location at Lehigh Valley International Airport, bringing its total network to 88 training centers. The school offers an accelerated program for students to earn airline pilot certifications. The curriculum is designed to be completed in approximately nine months.

research.title: A Dynamic Model and Stability Analysis of a Grid-Interactive Data Center
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid growth of data centers is creating new interactions between computational workload and power-system dynamics, with potentially significant implications for grid stability. We develop a four-dimensional nonlinear dynamical model of a data center campus interconnected. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: A physics-based reduced-order model unifies curved-meniscus inertia, viscous losses and nonsmooth contact-line stick-slip in a passive port-Hamiltonian formulation for lateral sloshing in cylindrical tanks. Dirichlet-Neumann and Jacobi operators describe inertia and restoring forces, while a convex. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: A probabilistic analysis of the Brumadinho tailings dam-breach using uncertainty quantification and global sensitivity analysis
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: On 25th January 2019, Dam B1 in Brumadinho, Brazil, suddenly collapsed and produced a catastrophic tailings flow with severe human, environmental and infrastructural consequences. Previous numerical back-analyses of the tailings flow have relied on deterministic approaches. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: ADSPICE: A Method of Automatic Differentiation for Gradient-Based Lumped Circuit Optimization with Native SPICE
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: This work presents a novel computer-aided design (CAD) tool for gradient-based circuit optimization using SPICE and automatic differentiation, which we term ADSPICE. Automatic differentiation (AD) is a technique for evaluating a derivative by breaking it into. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Adaptive Guidance for 3GPP Ambient IoT Contention-Based Random Access
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: The emerging ambient Internet of Things (A-IoT) envisions connectivity among large populations of low-cost, energy-constrained devices. Supporting such connectivity requires efficient coordination of device access, particularly in reader-triggered operation, where multiple devices may respond to paging. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Adaptive Line Switching for Cascade Mitigation in Power Systems via Graph Reinforcement Learning
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Although cascading failures are relatively rare events in power systems, they pose significant risks and can lead to severe economic and societal consequences within a short period. Therefore, developing effective mitigation strategies to prevent cascade propagation. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
